question.prompt:
In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB = AC = 28\) and \(BC = 20.\) Points \(D,\) \(E,\) and \(F\) are on sides \(\overline{AB},\) \(\overline{BC},\) and \(\overline{AC},\) respectively, such that \(\overline{DE}\) and \(\overline{EF}\) are parallel to \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{AB},\) respectively. What is the perimeter of parallelogram \(ADEF?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2013_AMC_12A_Q09_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so the perimeter of \(ADEF\) is \(2(AD+DE)\). To find this sum, compare \(DE\) with the remaining part \(DB\) of side \(AB\).

Since \(AB=AC\), triangle \(ABC\) has equal base angles:
\[
\angle ABC=\angle BCA.
\]
Because \(D\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\) and \(E\) lies on \(\overline{BC}\), \(\angle DBE=\angle ABC\). Also, \(DE\parallel AC\) gives \(\angle BED=\angle BCA\). Hence \(\angle DBE=\angle BED\), so the sides opposite these equal angles in triangle \(BDE\) are equal: \(DE=DB\).

Substituting this equality joins the two parts of \(AB\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Perimeter of }ADEF
&=2(AD+DE)\\
&=2(AD+DB)\\
&=2AB=2\cdot28=56.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the perimeter is \(\boxed{56}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
